correctness.rationale: All parameters and projections are explicit. On 1⊥, the exact Laplacian complement relation yields a Neumann remainder of ℓ1 norm at most 16r²/N³. Explicit three-level enumeration and subtraction of all deleted edges give TV_G(h0)=2+(2r-2c-2)/N-[2r(r+1)+2(r-c)(r-c+3)+T]/N², where 0≤T≤4r². This gives the 32r²/N² bound on Q columns; the exact diagonal-resistance identity gives the 44r²/N² bound on P columns. Integer codegree separation proves that every maximizing edge has minimal codegree when N>44r². Reconstructed 606 exact-rational columns across 11 graphs corroborate (but do not replace) this proof.

value.rationale: The result is a uniform sharp-order first-order law for a natural perturbation of a complete graph, depending on a genuinely local statistic not fixed by degree. It proves an all-graph structural rule for which edge orbits can carry the largest absolute transfer-current columns, with quantitative density threshold and nontrivial consequences for dense complements of cycles and hypercubes. It is broader than a table or parameter-specific recomputation, and the proof is self-contained.
